def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    # Priority is higher for smaller positive remaining capacity.
    # Use negative infinity for overflows to ensure they are last.
    priority_scores = np.where(remaining >= 0, remaining, -np.inf)
    # Invert so smallest positive remaining gets highest priority.
    # For exact fit (remaining == 0), priority becomes 0 (highest after inversion).
    # We want exact fit to be best, then larger remaining values lower.
    # Since we use remaining directly, smaller remaining is better.
    # To make higher score mean better, take negative of remaining.
    # But we already set overflows to -inf; handle separately.
    priority_scores = np.where(priority_scores != -np.inf, -priority_scores, -np.inf)
    return priority_scores
